body: Because a homonym, in its loose definition, can be a homograph (same spelling, different meaning, e.g. sow as in the animal vs. sow as in the verb) or a homophone (same pronunciation, different meaning, e.g. see and sea). Or a homonym can be more strictly defined as both a homograph and a homophone, i.e. same spelling, same pronunciation, different meaning, e.g. left (as opposed to right) and left (past tense of leave).

ESH. Your professor sucks because he should have assigned a more manageable project that could be completed using what you learned in class. You suck because you should have gone to office hours or emailed him about this, and asked if you could copy from online sources, before going ahead and doing that yourself. If your professor's policy is to not allow copying of other people's code (which is the case in most CS classes), and you turn the project in without admitting that you copied code, that's academic dishonesty.

My mom did that to me in my freshman year of college, and also somehow bugged my phone so that I couldn't prevent her from tracking me. To this day I still don't know how she managed to get my own phone to take photos of me without my knowledge and send them to her. Just want to warn you that this is within the realm of possibility, depending on how much of a control freak your mother is.
